name: worker.workflow
title: Portable durable workflow class execution
description:
Portable worker.workflow class ABI; supplements worker.runtime@1.1.0 without changing its plain-object default export, handlers, globals or environment. All documents use create's data-only rules; undefined is absent only for an entire optional document. Instance status is exactly queued, running, sleeping, waiting, complete, errored or terminated. Instances are runtime data, not Resources. Retained ids cannot be reused; terminal records and ids remain retained for 2592000 seconds.

Each fresh context selects the deployment's THEN-CURRENT weighted WorkerVersion and pins it for that context. Replay rebuilds context and class; fields, closures, module state and Promises do not survive. Step effects are at-least-once with memoized outcomes; an uncommitted effect may repeat after process death. Callbacks must be idempotent; code outside steps, including module evaluation and constructors, must be side-effect-free and deterministic against history. Deployment changes must remain compatible with in-flight histories.

The Host stops code before publishing sleeping, waiting or any terminal state; no context remains parked. Nothing runs after the absolute 31536000-second lifetime cutoff. Bounds and infrastructure interruptions are Host control, never catchable app sentinels. Step success is durably saved before resolution; first resolution and replay return decoded persisted clones, not the original result object. Invalid/oversized callback results are failed attempts under the saved retry policy; invalid/oversized final run output is run_threw.

step is bound to this context and instance; the app never passes instanceId. Steps are sequential. A second overlapping call, ANY run settlement while a step is unsettled, or incomplete cross-kind name reuse causes uncatchable step_definition_mismatch, ahead of run_threw. Stop precedes terminal publication; no mismatch rejection reaches app catch/finally. Its operation-error listing is an outcome, not a catchable Error. Finished names, including failed ones, replay by name regardless of new kind, without new effects; sleep discards a recorded success value. Validate the name before finished-history lookup, then ignore unused arguments for finished names. For a new/pending name, validate the listed argument positions and closed option schemas before new writes/effects; invalid JS calls reject with TypeError. An omitted optional argument may also be undefined. Pending same-kind calls use their first saved configuration, not valid new options. Names/types contain 1-256 Unicode scalar values. All state changes are ordered per (DurableWorkflow resource, instance id); matching events use acceptance order.

The Host owns the instance journal, event inbox, wake scheduling and execution fence. One owner may run an instance at a time; every commit checks its current fence, and a stale context cannot commit, use a Host-mediated effect, or publish state. External effects remain at-least-once and require application idempotency. Wakes/retries may repeat but acquire one fenced owner before code runs. State changes and event consumption are atomic and visible to status only after they commit. A terminated, completed, errored or expired instance cannot be resumed. The Host must retire the old execution context before exposing a terminal state or handing the instance to a new owner.

Host step Errors have an own, non-enumerable, non-writable, non-configurable name equal to the exact code. Provenance is private and bound to the exact object and context, not an app property. Rethrowing the same object preserves provenance; copying names or wrapping errors does not. Other fields may be annotated. Only an uncaught error privately branded step_failed promotes a run failure to terminal step_failed. All other uncaught errors, including branded wait_timeout and TypeError, are run_threw. Handling a step failure may still lead to complete.

operations.name: create
operations.description: Start one instance; id is optional and scoped to this DurableWorkflow. Commit queued state before replying; a retained id fails instance_exists. A minted id is not a safe retry key; choose a stable id when retrying an uncertain create. No serving deployment fails unsupported_capability. All documents (params, step results, event payloads, run output) have a plain or null-prototype object root with at most 1024 properties and 1048576 RFC 8785 canonical UTF-8 bytes. Nested values are null, booleans, finite numbers, Unicode-scalar strings, such objects, or dense ordinary arrays. Refuse accessors, symbols, array holes or extra properties, other prototypes, cycles, functions, BigInt, and nested undefined. Shared acyclic objects are allowed. Inspect descriptors; do not invoke getters or toJSON. Invalid params fail invalid_params; byte overflow fails document_too_large.

operations.name: get
operations.description: Resolve the handle of one retained instance. It fails unknown_instance when no instance holds the id — including one whose retention has passed — rather than minting an empty handle, so a consumer can tell a forgotten execution from a live one.

operations.name: status
operations.description: Read a retained instance. Output occurs only on complete and error only on errored. The closed error reasons are run_threw, step_failed, step_limit_exceeded, lifetime_exceeded and step_definition_mismatch. Workflow failure is a successful status read, not an operation rejection. Read a committed snapshot; never expose a parked or terminal state before its execution context is retired.

operations.name: sendEvent
operations.description: JS: instance.sendEvent({type, payload?, eventId?}) durably admits one event before resolving. eventId is an optional instance-scoped idempotency key. Retain its first accepted type and canonical payload fingerprint after consumption, until the record expires. Repeating the same key and canonical event succeeds without enqueueing, including after terminal; different content under the key fails event_conflict. Deduplicate before checking terminal. Retain type and canonical payload digest, not the consumed payload, for keyed deduplication. Unkeyed retries may duplicate. Consume matches in acceptance order. Retain at most 1024 unconsumed events per instance; a new event at that bound fails event_queue_full without acceptance. A new event after terminal fails instance_terminal. Admission and terminal transition serialize. Transport/backend interruption leaves acceptance unknown; keyed retry settles it. Keys are retained only for this instance record; no retry guarantee survives its expiry or id reuse.

operations.name: terminate
operations.description: JS: instance.terminate() stops an active instance, fences and retires its execution context, then commits terminated before resolving. It discards pending events and wakes. If already complete, errored or terminated, it succeeds without changing that terminal status. Concurrent completion and termination serialize; exactly one terminal outcome is visible. No continuation may commit an effect or state after terminal publication.

operations.name: run
operations.description: The main module's className named export must be constructible with a callable prototype run in every weighted version before Ready. No vendor base class or native context is required. Per fresh context use ordinary ECMAScript instance = new Export(env), then resolve instance.run and call it once with this=instance and (event, step). env is exactly that selected version's resolved worker.runtime@1.1.0 environment, never Host-private controls. event has exactly instanceId and params only if supplied at create; mutations are not durable. run returns a data-only object or undefined, directly or by Promise, not {output}. The schema wrapper is an observation only. Construction, run lookup/call, missing/non-callable execution-time run and uncaught failures yield run_threw, except genuine step_failed provenance and Host-controlled outcomes described above. Save a valid output before complete.

operations.name: stepDo
operations.description: JS: step.do(name, effect, retryPolicy?) returns Promise<object|undefined>, not {result}. effect is a zero-argument callable. Save normalized policy before the first callback: omission means maxAttempts=1; supplied policy requires maxAttempts (1-100 including first). initialDelaySeconds defaults to 0, backoff to constant, maxDelaySeconds to 43200; delays are integers 0-43200. After failed attempt k (one-based), delay is min(maxDelaySeconds,initialDelaySeconds) for constant or min(maxDelaySeconds,initialDelaySeconds*2^(k-1)) for exponential, capped without overflow. Every attempt uses the saved policy and calls effect once. Throw, rejection or invalid/oversized result fails that attempt. If retry remains, persist progress/due time, stop and replay in a fresh context not earlier than due, even for zero delay. Otherwise journal step_failed before rejecting with that Host Error. Commit success before resolving. Finished-name replay follows the common rules.

operations.name: stepSleep
operations.description: JS: step.sleep(name, seconds) returns Promise<void>. seconds is an integer 0-maxSleepSeconds. First registration saves duration and due time; replay keeps those values. A future sleep stops this context before sleeping becomes visible; its Promise never resolves there. At or after due time, a new context replays and durably completes the step before resolving undefined. A zero sleep commits and resolves in the current context. A sleep beyond the absolute lifetime stops with lifetime_exceeded, never a shortened sleep. Finished-name replay discards a recorded success value or rethrows its recorded step Error.

operations.name: stepWaitForEvent
operations.description: JS: step.waitForEvent(name, {type, timeoutSeconds}) returns Promise<object|undefined>, not {payload}. type and integer timeoutSeconds (1-maxWaitTimeoutSeconds) are required. First registration fixes type and absolute timeout. Atomically consume one retained matching event with step completion; an event already committed when timeout is decided and accepted no later than its deadline wins, even at the same timestamp, and cannot satisfy two waits. A retained eligible event resolves after commit in this context. Otherwise stop before publishing waiting; that Promise never resolves there. A new context replays to resolve the consumed payload, or durably records wait_timeout before rejecting with that Host Error. Absolute instance lifetime wins even if timeout is later. Finished-name replay follows the common rules.
